##### fm27-transfer-offers.md
# FM27: transfer offers, and contracts that are not in force yet

Where the game keeps a bid for a player, the contract he is offered, and a move agreed for a later day. RootTourist
worked it out on the Windows Steam build 26340721 (#81), following eleven players day by day in a VfB Stuttgart save
of July 2028 against the game's screens, and one transfer from the bid to the move. heval99 read it on a second save
of 169,023 players (#117). It was read again on the Windows Game Pass build 0.9.2435.0, on a save of 12 January 2028:
633 offers and 1,045 entries, joined to each other and to the players' running contracts.

The editor reads none of this yet. Nothing here was written to.

## A contract that is not in force yet

Every contract offered or agreed is an object of its own: a `db::FULL_CONTRACT`, or a `db::LOAN_CONTRACT` for a loan,
laid out as a running contract (the player's person block at `+0x08`, the team at `+0x10`, the wage at `+0x20`, the
start at `+0x44`, the end at `+0x48`, the squad status at `+0x54`, the kind at `+0xC3`). The player points only at
his running one (`+0x330`). `fmlibre-probe instances db::FULL_CONTRACT --holds <his person block> --span 0x10` finds
them all.

Jordy Makengo of Freiburg had three on the Game Pass save: his running contract (43,188 a week, since 19.2.2027, to
30.6.2031), the one Stuttgart offered him after Freiburg took their bid of 11,096,419 (44,082 a week, from 9.1.2028 to
30.6.2031), and a new one from Freiburg (51,138 a week, from 10.1.2028 to 30.6.2032).

## The entries

Each such contract is held by an entry of `0x48` bytes. The entries lie one after another in one run of memory.

| Offset | Type | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x00` | `u32` | 1 in every entry |
| `+0x10` | pointer | the contract; null in many entries (360 of the 1,045 on Game Pass), which are to be left out |
| `+0x20` | pointer | set only when the human manager's club is the one the player would join (RootTourist); set in none with a contract on Game Pass |
| `+0x28` | `i32` | the number of the transfer offer it came from (`FULL_TRANSFER_OFFER +0x5C`); -1 for a contract at his own club |
| `+0x3E` | `u8` | state: 1 offered, 2 agreed and waiting for its day, 3 turned down or lost; 4 in two entries |
| `+0x3F` | `u8` | 1 in every entry |
| `+0x40` | `u8` | 0 while offered and once lost, 1 once agreed (2 in 23 agreed entries, 5 in one) |
| `+0x41` | `u8` | kind (below) |

The kinds, with the 685 entries that have a contract on Game Pass:

| `+0x41` | What it is | Entries | What they hold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | a contract at his own club: a renewal, a youngster's first professional contract | 396 | all with his own club, none with an offer's number |
| 7 | a move without a fee | 103 | all with another club; the offer has no selling team in any, a fee in one |
| 2 | a transfer | 31 | all with another club; the offer has a selling team, and a fee in 25 |
| 1 | a loan, and also a transfer | 104 | 20 loan contracts; 83 full contracts with another club, Makengo's among them |
##### fm27-youth-intake.md
# FM27: youth intakes, the players the game makes, cities of birth

Read on the Game Pass build 0.9.2435.0 (a save of 16 January 2028, 10,837 players) with the probe (`column`,
`histogram`, `ties --all`, `player`, `youth`). What the Scouting tab's Youth intake section is built on
(`crates/fmlibre-core/src/youth_intake.rs`).

## The players the game made

The byte before the gender flags in the identity block (`player +0x2A0` on Windows, 0x18 into it) holds a flag
`0x08` for a player the game made. It was set for 1,783 players, 16.2 years old on average, and they were exactly
the players with a UID from 2,002,068,314 up: the game numbers the people it makes itself, in the order it makes
them, after the database's own. The rest of the byte read 0, 1, 2 and 4 on others (1 for players of 35.8 on average,
which this note does not name), and `0x40` is set for 43 of the game's players.

Players of the database have UIDs up to about 2,001,000,000 (newer real players included), so a UID says nothing
for sure; the flag does.

`player +0x36C` (u32) is `-1` for 1,823 players: the 1,783 and 40 players of the database (Japanese and Chilean
clubs' players added to the database late, such as Sota Nakamura of Sanfrecce Hiroshima). Other players hold a
number of their own there (Toni Micevski 1,947). It is not used.

On the Mac the identity block is laid out alike (`gender = 0x3A1` there), so the flag is at `0x3A0` (see "On the
Mac" below).

## A club's youth intake

The game keeps no list of a club's intakes. On the day of a nation's intake, every club of it with a youth setup gets
its players: they join it that day, at 15 or 16 (a few at 17), and all of them share the day of joining in their
contract (`[contract] joined`). On the save:

- Fenerbahçe's intake of 11 March 2027: twelve players, UIDs 2,002,069,121 to 2,002,069,132, all born in 2011; one
  of them, Ahmet Beytaş, is on loan at Yalova FK. In January 2028 all twelve held full-time contracts (kind 1), some
  signed later than the intake (Osman Sütlü's on 28 September 2027), all of them joined on 11 March 2027.
- The largest days: 7 April 2027 (152 players at 140 clubs), 10 March 2027 (119 players), 20 March 2027 (96). A day
  of 14 January 2028 (52 players, 29 clubs, two days before the save's date) still had youth contracts and no ties at
  all.
- 421 of the game's players had no club: youth candidates the clubs let go.

A player the game made can leave his club: Engin Demirtas (Kasımpaşa's intake of 18 March 2027) joined Fenerbahçe on
21 August 2027, and Onuralp Balcıoğlu, let go by the club whose candidate he was, on 8 January 2028.

**The relations tell the first club apart** (see `fm27-nationality.md`): some time after the intake the game ties a
player to his club as one trained there (kind 72, with its homegrown rules), and to that club only. Engin Demirtas's
ties name Kasımpaşa, not Fenerbahçe. Onuralp Balcıoğlu has no tie to a club: he began his career at Fenerbahçe. The
players of 14 January 2028 had no tie yet.

##### fm27-gamepass-0.9.2355.md
# FM27 Game Pass build 0.9.2355.0 (Launch Preview)

Observed on 2026-10-30 from the installed package
`SportsInteractive.FootballManager27_0.9.2355.0_x64__5w3tn6tb6stnm`
under `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\`. The full release (2026-11-10) will be a
different build; re-check everything here against it.

## Install

- GDK (MSIXVC) package: `MicrosoftGame.config`, `gamelaunchhelper.exe`,
  `libHttpClient.GDK.dll`, `PlayFabMultiplayerGDK.dll`, `Party.dll`, `XCurl.dll`.
- Entry point `GameLaunchHelper.exe` (`runFullTrust`, not an AppContainer); the
  running process is `fm.exe`.
- `fm.exe` cannot be read from disk (ACL protected). Every other file can, which is
  all the editor needs.

## Engine

- Unity `6000.3.18f1-custom`, IL2CPP backend.
- `fm_Data/il2cpp_data/Metadata/global-metadata.dat`: not encrypted, metadata
  version 39 (`AF 1B B1 FA 27 00 00 00`). The original Il2CppDumper rejects v39; use
  Cpp2IL or a v39 fork.
- Managed names are not obfuscated (`SI.UI`, `SI.Bindable`, `FM.GamePlugin`,
  `SI.Interop`, `FM.Match`, ...).
- `GameAssembly.dll` exports 241 `il2cpp_*` API functions.
- `fm_Data/il2cpp_data/il2cpp.usym` (87 MB) ships too.

## Native game core: `fm_Data/Plugins/x86_64/game_plugin.dll`

- 423 MB on disk. Section names are rewritten and code sits outside `.text`
  (`.text` 4 KB, `.debug` 327 MB, `.trace` 78 MB, `.xpdata`, `.xtext`, `.xtls`,
  `.sdata`, `.sbss`, ...): anti-tamper protection. FM26 used Denuvo.
- The Steam build of the same module uses different section names (`.srdata`,
  `.arch`, `.sdata`, `.code` per fm-editor's notes), so it is a different binary.
- 282 exports. The UI talks to the core through an `IGamePlugin` interface
  (`Initialise`, `Tick`, `OpenChannels`, `PerformChannelActions`, `SendEvent`,
  `UpdateChannelData`, `Shutdown`) and receives data through `IPluginDataReceiver`
  callbacks (`SendDataResponse`, `SendEvent`), plus `get_*_layout_signature`
  exports for marshalling checks. The managed side only mirrors what the UI shows;
  the full database is on the native heap.
- Export `game_plugin_plugin_build_timestamp` may serve as a build fingerprint.

## Steam reference layout (from fm-editor)

From [fm-editor's FM27 notes](https://github.com/barak14/fm-editor/blob/main/docs/fm27/memory-layout.md)
(Steam build; GPL-3.0-or-later). Entities live in heap arrays referenced by
`(begin, end)` pointer pairs in a writable section of `game_plugin.dll`; objects are
told apart by vtable.

| What | Steam RVA |
##### fm27-gamepass-0.9.2409.md
# FM27 Game Pass build 0.9.2409.0

Observed on 2 November 2026, right after the Xbox app installed this update. The package is
`SportsInteractive.FootballManager27_0.9.2409.0_x64__5w3tn6tb6stnm`, run from
`D:\Games\Football Manager 27\Content\`. The test save was on 9 September 2026, with 59,287 players, 29,512 staff
and 31,233 clubs.

In the app, the update showed up as a missing in-game date. With no date there were no ages, so the age column and
the profiles' ages were blank. Planned retirements were hidden too, because nothing placed the retirement manager.
Everything else read as before. `profiles/fm27/gamepass-0.9.2409.0.toml` now places all three.

## The binary

`game_plugin.dll` as mapped in memory:

| | 0.9.2409.0 | 0.9.2355.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Size of image | `0x175DA000` | `0x19436000` |
| Link timestamp | `0x6AE563A1` (31 October 2026) | `0x6ADFB161` (26 October 2026) |

The protector has renamed and reordered the sections again:
- the entity arrays' pairs, the in-game date and the classes' type descriptors are in `.00cfg` (read-write, 1 MiB at
  `0x55E9000`);
- the vtables are in `.trace` (read-only);
- the large read-write-execute section is `.rsrc` (282 MiB).

None of these names can be relied on from one build to the next.

## What moved

- **Entity arrays:** 0x2000 further than in 0.9.2355.0:
  - players at `0x5683DC0`;
  - staff at `0x5683E08`;
  - clubs at `0x5683F78`.

  With no profile, `calibrate` found them by scanning, and every sampled element decoded.
- **Retirement manager:** the static pointer is at `0x5675060`, still 0xED60 before the players pair. It is the only
  pointer to the one `RETIREMENT_MANAGER` object, which `instances` finds by its type name.
- **In-game date:** the date that sits with the arrays (`+0x848` from the players pair) read `01 00 6C 07` with the
  save loaded. That is day 1 of 1900, an unset date, so the reader gave no date at all.
  - The date is now a variable of its own, at `0x56257C8`. It reads `FC 3A EA 07`: day 252 of 2026 (the low 9 bits of
    `0x3AFC`), which is 9 September 2026. The game's UI held the text "9th September 2026" at the same time.
  - In the plugin's writable sections outside `.rsrc`, the only other date in 2026 is the database's timestamp. It
    sits at `+0x638` from the players pair (14 October 2026), as in 0.9.2355.0.
  - The arm64 Mac build keeps its date the same way (see the [macOS notes](fm27-steam-macos.md)). There, the field
    with the arrays stayed unset after a save was loaded, even once the game had moved on a day, while the variable
    followed the game. That was not watched over a day on this build.

## Unchanged

##### fm27-gamepass-0.9.2435.md
# FM27 Game Pass 0.9.2435.0 (the full release)

Observed on 10 November 2026, half an hour after the update to the full release, with the Game Pass package
`SportsInteractive.FootballManager27_0.9.2435.0_x64__5w3tn6tb6stnm`. The save, of 3 January 2028 (10,812 players,
9,359 staff and 19,775 clubs), had been read in full on 0.9.2409.0 the same day, right after loading it, and was read
again right after loading it on this build.

## The binary

`game_plugin.dll` as mapped in memory:

| | 0.9.2435.0 | 0.9.2409.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Size of image | `0x17969000` | `0x175DA000` |

# FM27 on macOS: the Steam build 26227640

Observed on 2026-10-31 on an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 27.0.1 and System Integrity
Protection on, from the Steam install under
`~/Library/Application Support/Steam/steamapps/common/Football Manager 27/` (app 4530370,
build 26227640, depot 4530373). Steam gives the Mac build the same build id as the Windows
one. The game had not been started on this Mac before; the layout below was then measured on
a new save (Tyrone Demarcus at Arsenal, 14 July 2026), with the game started by Steam through
the bridge's launcher.

## The app

`fm.app` is a Unity 6000.3.18f1 player, universal (arm64 and x86_64):

| | |
|---|---|
| Bundle id | `com.SportsInteractive.FootballManager27`, version 27.0.0.2486716 |
| Executable | `fm.app/Contents/MacOS/Football Manager 27`, the process name too |
| Game plugin | `fm.app/Contents/PlugIns/game_plugin.bundle/Contents/MacOS/game_plugin`, a Mach-O bundle |
| Other modules | `UnityPlayer.dylib` and `GameAssembly.dylib` in `Contents/Frameworks` |

`game_plugin` has a `LC_UUID` per architecture, which identifies the build as the PE header
does on Windows:

| | arm64 | x86_64 |
|---|---|---|
| `LC_UUID` | `9E8E47DE-F704-314C-917D-C32D12637678` | `22CFE5C3-B5CF-3C00-8043-1EA190A69B89` |

The arm64 image is `0x58F4000` bytes: `__TEXT` `0x54B0000`, `__DATA_CONST` `0x1F4000`,
`__DATA` `0x9C000` (with `__common` at `0x56D10D0` and `__bss` at `0x5721BA0`) and
`__LINKEDIT`. The `(begin, end)` pairs of the entity arrays are globals, so they should be in
`__DATA`; `calibrate --scan` scans the writable segments as it scans `.data` on Windows.

## Why macOS keeps the editor out

The app and `game_plugin` are signed by SEGA's Developer ID (`3JJX9QL35J`), notarized, and
built with the **hardened runtime**. Their entitlements:

```text
com.apple.security.cs.allow-dyld-environment-variables   true
com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation         true
com.apple.security.device.camera                         true
com.apple.security.personal-information.photos-library   true
```

...
## The object layout

`calibrate` found the arrays where Windows has them relative to each other: players at
`game_plugin+0x5C891C8` (38,007, the same as the Windows Steam test save), staff `0x48` and
clubs `0x1B8` after them. With the Windows layout no name decoded, as clang lays classes with
virtual bases out by the Itanium C++ ABI, not MSVC's. `profiles/fm27/layout-macos.toml` holds
the Mac offsets:

| | Windows | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Player's own fields (positions, attributes, CA/PA, condition, morale, team, injuries) | | 8 bytes earlier: no vbptr |
| Person (names, nation, personality, birth date, contract, caps) | after the identity block, `+0x2B0` | first, `+0x278`; its fields 0x40 earlier |
| Identity block (UID; what contracts and captaincies point at) | `+0x288`, before the person | `+0x388`, after it |
| Player-coach shift | `0xF8` | `0xF8` (Paul Ifill's UID at `+0x48C`) |
| Staff's own fields (attributes, reputation, CA/PA) | | the same |
| Staff person / identity block | `+0x128` / `+0x100` | `+0xF8` / `+0x208` |
| Human manager shift | `0x340` | `0x340` (the save's own manager) |
| In-game date | `+0x848` from the players pair | a variable of its own (below) |

Contracts, clubs, club info, club finances, teams, nations and injuries are laid out as on
Windows. Witnesses on the running game:

- Lionel Messi: born 24 June 1987, 207 caps and 125 goals, 18 and 14 for the U21s, his
  positions and attributes, a contract that ends on 31 December 2028 with squad number 10.
- Tottenham Hotspur: 50,000 season tickets, founded 1882, supporter traits 18/14/7/14/7/14,
  £65 tickets, corporate facilities 20, reputation 7650; captain Micky van de Ven and
  vice-captain Pedro Porro, whose captaincies point at their identity blocks.
- Injuries: David Wotherspoon's moderate calf muscle strain, among others.

With the build profile of the Intel half, `calibrate` decoded 100% of the sampled players,
staff and clubs. The probe then wrote, read back and restored right away: Messi's finishing,
his ambition and his squad number; Pedro Porro as Tottenham's captain (the two captains
swap); Mikel Arteta's tactical attribute; Tottenham's balance; and a swap of Ben Davies with
Tom Heaton (14 writes).

## Natively, on Apple silicon

Started again from Steam through the native-first launcher, FM27 (pid 17731) ran natively,

def build() -> dict:
    docs = []
    for name in sorted(DIGEST):
        path = RECON / name
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        lines = text.splitlines()
        points = [{"line": ln, "point": pt} for ln, pt in DIGEST[name]]
        docs.append(
            {
                "doc": name,
                "title": lines[0].lstrip("# ").strip(),
                "line_count": len(lines),
                "sections": [ln.strip() for ln in lines if ln.startswith("## ")],
                "key_points": points,
                "key_point_count": len(points),
            }
        )
    return {
        "schema": "t93/fm27_recon_digest/v1",
        "provenance": PROVENANCE,
        "method": "read-only digest of docs/recon/*.md; every point carries its source line",
        "grade_policy": "external reference only; never our L1-L4 grade",
        "doc_count": len(docs),
        "point_total": sum(d["key_point_count"] for d in docs),
        "docs": docs,
    }


def selftest() -> int:
    data = build()
    assert data["doc_count"] >= 20, data["doc_count"]
    assert (RECON / "fm27-bans.md").is_file()
    on_disk = sorted(p.name for p in RECON.glob("*.md"))
    assert on_disk == sorted(d["doc"] for d in data["docs"]), set(on_disk) ^ set(
        d["doc"] for d in data["docs"]
    )
    for d in data["docs"]:
        assert 3 <= d["key_point_count"] <= 8, (d["doc"], d["key_point_count"])
        lines = (RECON / d["doc"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        for p in d["key_points"]:
            assert 1 <= p["line"] <= len(lines), (d["doc"], p["line"])
            assert lines[p["line"] - 1].strip(), (d["doc"], p["line"])
    print("selftest OK:", data["doc_count"], "docs,", data["point_total"], "points")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.selftest:
        return selftest()
    data = build()
    text = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + "\n"
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print("wrote", args.out, data["doc_count"], "docs")
    else:
        print(text[:1500])
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
